successor: Kingdom of Portugal (Braganza crown; court in Rio de Janeiro from 1808; United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves from 1815)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'John VI, king of Portugal', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/print/article/304822
source2: Kirsten Schultz, Tropical Versailles: Empire, Monarchy, and the Portuguese Royal Court in Rio de Janeiro, 1808-1821, Routledge 2001 - https://scholarship.shu.edu/history-publications/26
notes: 1806 marks no break. Junot's French army occupied Lisbon Nov 1807 to Aug 1808, but the Prince Regent and government moved to Rio and continued; British-Portuguese forces expelled the French in 1808. Database end date looks arbitrary.

source2: Boubacar Barry, 'Bokar Biro and the conquest of Futa Jallon', in Senegambia and the Atlantic Slave Trade, Cambridge University Press 1997 - https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/senegambia-and-the-atlantic-slave-trade/bokar-biro-and-the-conquest-of-futa-jallon/F6FD3D6C54521DF6D79F74A22F278EE3
notes: France encircled Futa Jallon, then used armed force from 1896; French troops occupied Timbo in 1896 and the state became part of French Guinea. Q4: severe internal crisis, with Alfaya/Soriya rivals and provincial chiefs opposing almamy Bokar Biro.

successor: Pandyan (South Indian) rulers at Anuradhapura: Pandu and successors
source1: U.S. Library of Congress, Sri Lanka: A Country Study, 'Rise of Sinhalese and Tamil Ethnic Awareness' - https://countrystudies.us/sri-lanka/6.htm
notes: After Mahanama there were brief, violent reigns (a minister installed a puppet king, Mittasena). Pandyan invaders under Pandu then killed Mittasena and ruled Anuradhapura for about 25 years, until Dhatusena (459-77) restored Sinhalese rule. Dates vary by chronology (c.429-436).

successor: British Empire II (same United Kingdom state, London)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Victoria, queen of United Kingdom', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Victoria-queen-of-United-Kingdom
notes: 1849 is only a database period split: the Crown and government in London continued under Victoria (1837-1901). Q4: Irish Great Famine 1845-49 (about 1 million dead) and Chartist agitation. The database's home area 'Deccan' looks wrong.

successor: Koktepe I / Early Iron Age oasis cultures of Sogdiana (Yaz I horizon)
source1: E. de La Vaissiere, 'Sogdiana iii. History and Archeology', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/sogdiana-iii-history-and-archeology
notes: An archaeological culture with no recorded central authority. Iranica says Kok Tepe was occupied from at least the 15th c. BCE through the Iron Age, which suggests settlement continuity in Sogdiana. No replacement is documented. Inference only.

successor: Indo-Scythians (Saka: Maues and Azes dynasty at Taxila; satrap Rajuvula in eastern Punjab)
notes: Saka kings took Taxila (Maues c.80s BCE, Azes I c.50s BCE). Saka satrap Rajuvula supplanted the last Indo-Greek kings, Strato II/III in eastern Punjab, c.10 CE. The kingdom had fragmented among rival kings. Database end of -10 is approximate.

successor: Middle Elamite Kingdom (Shutrukid dynasty: Shutruk-Nahhunte, Kutir-Nahhunte)
source1: Francois Vallat, 'Elam i. The history of Elam', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-i
notes: Shutruk-Nahhunte killed Zababa-shuma-iddina (1158) and put Kutir-Nahhunte on Babylon's throne; Kutir-Nahhunte deposed Enlil-nadin-ahi (1157-55), ending the dynasty. Q4: Britannica and Zadok note late provincial detachment and local insurrection, timing vague.

successor: Anuradhapura kingdom under the Lambakanna dynasty (Vasabha)
source1: The Mahavamsa, ch. 35 'The Twelve Kings', English translation (apparently W. Geiger, Pali Text Society 1912) - https://lakdiva.org.lk/mahavamsa/chap035.html
source2: Sirima Kiribamune, 'Tamils in Ancient and Medieval Sri Lanka: The Historical Roots of Ethnic Identity', Ethnic Studies Report IV/1, 1986 - https://thuppahis.com/2021/05/03/tamils-in-ancient-and-medieval-sri-lanka-the-historical-roots-of-ethnic-identity/
notes: The Lambakanna Vasabha defeated the usurper Subharaja in battle (c.67 CE) and took sovereignty in the same capital: a dynastic change inside the state. Q4: Lambakannas deposed Ilanaga, who retook the throne with foreign troops; Subha usurped c.60.

source1: Francois Vallat, 'Elam i. The history of Elam', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-i
notes: After Shilhina-hamru-Lagamar (c.1100), Vallat says no Elamite document gives historical information for about 250 years; Britannica says nothing is known for almost 300 years. No event at 900 BCE is documented, so the database boundary is unsupported.

source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Tiberius-Sempronius-Gracchus
notes: 133 BCE (Tiberius Gracchus's tribunate and killing) is a period marker; the Republic's institutions continued until 27 BCE. Q4: First Servile War in Sicily, 135-132 BCE (Eunus, about 70,000 slaves; Britannica 'Eunus').
